description: Ops delivered after their connection ended (MCPWARP.md §2.7 Ended connection, §5.9; CLIENT-SDK.md Handler delivery row): each flush_after op was received on the connection before the 4012 close but is delivered to the mcpwarp layer AFTER the disconnect notification. A disable delivered that way is ignored, so the status is connecting/DISCONNECTED (T30), never disabled, and the reconnect goes online. A conflict delivered the same way still applies, because conflict is sticky (and is not a superseded connection's op, T38): conflict/TAKEN_OVER, and no reconnect during a long tick. The fixture depends on that delivery order: a runner that cannot force the disconnect notification ahead of the flushed ops MUST skip it with a note (runnerRequirement).

expect.lastError: Another connection took over this name.
